P1.reason: B lumps the whole game into one group, so no rules come out of it. A's groups are imperfect and overlap, but they roughly follow moves, outcome, doors and turns.

differences.reason: Helps a little: collects legal moves and observation, but too broad, mixing all phases and stray next rules.
Helps: car persistence, final choice and win conditions form a recognizable winning rule.
Helps: doors plus hiding and choosing form a sensible first-step rule.
Helps: step sequence and termination is a clear turn-order rule, though car/chosen statements intrude.
Helps: doors start closed and close-state update form a coherent door-opening state rule.
Helps: the switch-or-stay rule is the key mechanic, cleanly isolated.
Neutral: roles are setup, a minor but acceptable group.
Hurts: one all-statement group gives no division into rules at all.
